instantiated_cells.justification: Section 101.73(A) requires each legislative agent to file a statement of expenditures with the updated registration statement.
Updated registration statements (with expenditure statements) are due by the last day of January, May, and September—three times per year.
Expenditure statements are filed with the updated registration statement, which is due three times per year (Jan/May/Sep).
The statute specifies updated filings in January, May, and September rather than a single annual filing cadence.
The filing months are January, May, and September, which is not quarterly (four times per year).
The statute mandates three filings per year, not two.
No monthly filing is described; instead filings occur three times per year.
The statute specifies a triannual schedule and does not provide an alternative 'other' cadence.
A legislative agent’s statement must show the total amount of expenditures made during the reporting period.

When expenditures are made for/benefit specified officials (and for meals over the annual threshold), the statement must include the recipient name, total amount, description, approximate date, and related legislation/client.
The required disclosures for particular officials require itemization elements (recipient, amount, description, date, and legislation/client) rather than only aggregate totals.
The statute requires a brief description of expenditures and defines expenditure types, but it does not require categorizing expenditures into statutory type categories on the report.
Reportable 'expenditures' include gifts and items such as entertainment, lodging, and transportation, and such expenditures must be disclosed when made for the benefit of covered officials.
For itemized expenditures, the filer must disclose the 'specific items of legislation, if any,' for which the expenditures were made.

Updated registration statements must list the specific bills or resolutions on which the agent actively advocated, and expenditure itemizations must identify the specific items of legislation, if any.
The statute requires expenditure disclosure by recipient (and related legislation/client), not aggregated totals per issue area across recipients.
General issue/type-of-legislation descriptions are required in the initial registration statement, but the expenditure statement provisions do not require reporting general issues.
Expenditure statements call for descriptions, dates, recipients, and specific legislation/client, but do not require reporting general subject matter categories.
Section 101.73 governs expenditures and does not require disclosure of lobbying contacts made.
The statement must identify legislation and client but does not require stating support/oppose position on the legislation.
The expenditure statement content requirements do not include the legislative agent’s address or other contact information.
For itemized expenditures, the filer must report 'the identity of the client on whose behalf each expenditure was made,' which provides the principal/client name.
While client identity is required for certain expenditures, the statute does not require listing the client's address or other contact information on the expenditure statement.
No provision in the expenditure statement requirements asks for the nature of the principal's business.

The statute expressly excludes 'compensation paid to legislative agents' from the definition of expenditures for employer statements and does not otherwise require reporting compensation amounts in expenditure statements.

Because compensation paid to legislative agents is excluded from reportable expenditures and no compensation reporting requirement appears, there is no requirement to break compensation down by payer.
Each legislative agent must file a statement of expenditures with each updated registration statement due triannually, and the statute does not provide an exception for zero expenditures.
The expenditure definition covers expenditures made for the benefit of specified officials and staff, but does not include their household or family members.
